payload.statement: The Pauli spectrum is reinterpreted as the energy spectrum of a fictitious many-body system. Perspective 1 builds the stabilizer Hamiltonian $\hat H(\psi)=\sum_{P,s}(1-s\tr(\psi P))|P,s)(P,s|$ on $\mathcal{H}_n^{\otimes2}\otimes\mathbb{C}^2$, with a $|{\rm Stab}(\psi)|$-fold degenerate ground level and parity block structure. Perspective 2 treats each Pauli as a two-level particle with energies $E_{P,\pm}=1\pm\tr[\psi_AP]$, giving $d^2$ particles in the band $[0,2]$, the Pauli gas. The asserted dictionary is that stabilizer states give a maximally rigid gas with only the integer levels $\{0,1,2\}$ and ground degeneracy $d$, while magic populates fractional interior levels and depletes the degenerate ground level.

components.text: Nonstabilizerness, a microscopic property of $\psi_A$, is recast as a macroscopic spectral property of a thermodynamically large ensemble: stabilizer states give a rigid integer spectrum, magic populates fractional levels and depletes the ground degeneracy.

$\hat H(\psi)=\sum_{P\in\mathcal{P}_n,s\in\{-1,1\}}(1-s\,\tr(\psi P))|P,s)(P,s|$ has a $|{\rm Stab}(\psi)|$-fold degenerate ground level; it commutes with $\mathbb{I}^{\otimes2}\otimes\hat n$ and is block diagonal, $\hat H=\hat H_+\oplus\hat H_-$.
